# Function reference {#sec-reference}

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
source("_setup.R")
```

Every exported function, grouped the same way as the README. Each entry
gives the signature, every argument, the return value, and at least one
runnable example. This chapter is the detailed reference; @sec-quickstart
is the faster tour.

## Matching & substitution

### `fgrepl()`

Equivalent to `base::grepl()`, using PCRE2 and Intel TBB. Large inputs can
use multiple cores; the crossover depends on subject length and pattern
cost. See @sec-theory for how `perl = FALSE` follows base R's default
regex rules and how non-ASCII text is matched.
With `fixed = TRUE`, the byte-oriented pattern is prepared once: one-byte
needles use `memchr`, two- and three-byte needles use `memchr` plus
`memcmp`, and longer needles use Boyer–Moore–Horspool. `ignore.case = TRUE`
uses a 256-entry byte-folding table without lowercasing each input string.

```r
fgrepl(pattern, x, ignore.case = FALSE, perl = FALSE, fixed = FALSE,
       useBytes = FALSE, nthreads = NULL)
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `pattern` | Character scalar. Pattern to search for. |
| `x` | Character vector. `NA` elements return `NA`. |
| `ignore.case` | Logical. Case-insensitive matching. |
| `perl` | Logical. Use PCRE semantics instead of base R's default (TRE) rules. |
| `fixed` | Logical. Treat `pattern` as a literal string and use the prepared literal-search path. |
| `useBytes` | Logical. Match byte by byte rather than by UTF-8 character, as in base R. |
| `nthreads` | Positive integer per-call thread cap, or `NULL` for the RcppParallel default; `1` forces serial execution. |

**Returns:** logical vector the same length as `x`.

```{r}
fgrepl("^inv", c("invoice", "Invoice", "credit"), ignore.case = TRUE)
fgrepl("a.b", c("axb", "ab"), fixed = TRUE)  # literal "a.b" — no match for "axb"
```

### `fgrep()`

Equivalent to `base::grep()`: wraps `fgrepl()` and returns indices or
values.

```r
fgrep(pattern, x, ignore.case = FALSE, perl = FALSE, value = FALSE,
      fixed = FALSE, useBytes = FALSE, invert = FALSE, nthreads = NULL)
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `pattern`, `x`, `ignore.case`, `perl`, `fixed`, `useBytes`, `nthreads` | Same as `fgrepl()`. |
| `value` | Logical. Return matching elements instead of indices. |
| `invert` | Logical. Return non-matching indices/values instead. |

**Returns:** integer vector of indices, or a character vector when
`value = TRUE`.

```{r}
fgrep("^inv", c("invoice", "credit", "invoice2"))
fgrep("^inv", c("invoice", "credit", "invoice2"), value = TRUE)
```

### `fcount()`

No direct base R equivalent (the usual idiom is
`vapply(gregexpr(...), length, ...)`, which allocates a match-position
vector per element just to take its length). Counts **non-overlapping**
matches of one pattern in each element, using the same PCRE2 and
prepared-fixed-string engines and the same parallel dispatch as `fgrepl()`.

```r
fcount(pattern, x, ignore.case = FALSE, perl = FALSE, fixed = FALSE,
       useBytes = FALSE, nthreads = NULL)
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `pattern`, `x`, `ignore.case`, `perl`, `fixed`, `useBytes`, `nthreads` | Same as `fgrepl()`. |

**Returns:** integer vector the same length as `x`, with `names(x)`
preserved. `NA` elements return `NA`; elements with no match return `0L`.

An empty `pattern`, which has character-position semantics in base R, is
delegated to `base::gregexpr()`. After an empty match the search moves on
by one character, where `gregexpr(perl = TRUE)` moves on by one byte.

```{r}
fcount("[0-9]", c("a1b2c3", "none", NA))
fcount("aa", "aaaa", fixed = TRUE)   # 2 -- matches do not overlap

# Column-level data-quality rules, one vectorised call each
nm <- c("JOHN O'BRIEN", "UNKNOWN 00000000", "Kyle John Haynes")
fcount("[0-9]", nm)        # digits in a name field
fcount(" +", nm) + 1L      # token count
```

### `fsub()`

Equivalent to `base::sub()`: first-match substitution. Supports `\\1`-`\\9`
capture groups and `\\U`/`\\L`/`\\E` case conversion in `replacement`.

```r
fsub(pattern, replacement, x, ignore.case = FALSE, perl = FALSE,
     fixed = FALSE, useBytes = FALSE, nthreads = NULL)
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `pattern` | Character scalar. Pattern to search for. |
| `replacement` | Character scalar. Replacement string. |
| `x` | Character vector. `NA` elements return `NA`. |
| `ignore.case`, `perl`, `fixed`, `useBytes`, `nthreads` | Same as `fgrepl()`. |

**Returns:** character vector the same length as `x`.

```{r}
fsub("-([0-9]+)$", "_\\1", c("invoice-001", "invoice-002"))
```

### `fgsub()`

Equivalent to `base::gsub()`: global substitution. Same capture-group and
case-conversion support as `fsub()`.

```r
fgsub(pattern, replacement, x, ignore.case = FALSE, perl = FALSE,
      fixed = FALSE, useBytes = FALSE, nthreads = NULL)
```

Arguments are identical to `fsub()`. **Returns:** character vector the
same length as `x`.

```{r}
fgsub("[aeiou]", "_", c("hello world", "fast string"), ignore.case = TRUE)
```

### `gsub_all()`

No base R equivalent: applies several patterns in a single function call,
either sequentially (chained, like repeated `fgsub()` calls — later
patterns can match text introduced by earlier replacements) or, for
`fixed = TRUE`, as one combined left-to-right scan (`sequential = FALSE`).
Non-sequential regex replacement is rejected explicitly.

```r
gsub_all(patterns, replacements, x, fixed = FALSE, ignore.case = FALSE,
         sequential = TRUE, nthreads = NULL, perl = FALSE, useBytes = FALSE)
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `patterns` | Character vector of patterns to search for. |
| `replacements` | Character scalar or vector the same length as `patterns`. |
| `x` | Character vector. `NA` elements return `NA`. |
| `fixed` | Logical. Treat each pattern as a literal string. |
| `ignore.case` | Logical. Case-insensitive matching. |
| `sequential` | Logical (default `TRUE`). `TRUE` = chained passes; `FALSE` = fixed-pattern single combined scan. |
| `nthreads` | Positive integer per-call thread cap, or `NULL` for the RcppParallel default; `1` forces serial execution. |
| `perl` | Logical. As in `fgsub()`. |
| `useBytes` | Logical. As in `fgsub()`. |

**Returns:** character vector the same length as `x`.

```{r}
gsub_all(c("Mr\\.", "Mrs\\."), c("Mister", "Missus"), c("Mr. Smith", "Mrs. Jones"))
```

### `fextract()` / `fextract_all()`

The first match (or a capture group of it), or every non-overlapping match,
as `regmatches(x, regexpr(...))` / `regmatches(x, gregexpr(...))` or
`stringr::str_extract()` / `str_extract_all()` would return it. Patterns
follow `fgrepl()`'s rules; after an empty match the search moves on one
character, as in `fcount()`.

```r
fextract(pattern, x, ignore.case = FALSE, perl = FALSE, fixed = FALSE,
         useBytes = FALSE, group = 0L, nthreads = NULL)
fextract_all(pattern, x, ignore.case = FALSE, perl = FALSE, fixed = FALSE,
             useBytes = FALSE, group = 0L, nthreads = NULL)
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `pattern`, `x`, `ignore.case`, `perl`, `fixed`, `useBytes` | As in `fgrepl()`. |
| `group` | `0` for the whole match, `k` for capture group `k` (`NA` when the group did not take part). Must be `0` with `fixed = TRUE`. |
| `nthreads` | Positive integer per-call thread cap, or `NULL` for the RcppParallel default; `1` forces serial execution. |

**Returns:** `fextract()` a character vector (`NA` for no match);
`fextract_all()` a list of character vectors (`character(0)` for no match,
`NA` for a missing string). Both keep `names(x)`.

```{r}
x <- c("Unit 4, 12 Smith St", "PO Box 99", NA)
fextract("[0-9]+", x)
fextract_all("[0-9]+", x)
fextract("([0-9]+) ([A-Za-z]+) St", x, group = 2)
```

### `fgrepl_any()` / `fcount_any()` / `fwhich_any()` / `fextract_any()`

Searches for any of many literal strings in one pass with an Aho-Corasick
automaton, so thousands of keywords cost about as much as a few. Matches are
leftmost-first: the earliest match wins, and among matches at the same
position the pattern listed first. `fwhich_any()` returns the first pattern
(in the order of `patterns`) found anywhere in the string, which suits
priority-ordered keyword categories.

```r
fgrepl_any(patterns, x, ignore.case = FALSE, useBytes = FALSE, nthreads = NULL)
fcount_any(patterns, x, ignore.case = FALSE, useBytes = FALSE, nthreads = NULL)
fwhich_any(patterns, x, ignore.case = FALSE, useBytes = FALSE, nthreads = NULL)
fextract_any(patterns, x, all = FALSE, ignore.case = FALSE, useBytes = FALSE,
             nthreads = NULL)
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `patterns` | Literal strings to look for (no `NA` or `""`). |
| `x` | Character vector. `NA` elements return `NA`. |
| `ignore.case` | Fold ASCII letters, as `fgrepl(fixed = TRUE)` does. |
| `useBytes` | Match bytes rather than UTF-8 text. |
| `all` | `fextract_any()`: return every match (a list). |
| `nthreads` | Positive integer per-call thread cap, or `NULL` for the RcppParallel default; `1` forces serial execution. |

**Returns:** a logical vector, integer vectors, or the matched text (a
list with `all = TRUE`), the same length as `x`.

`gsub_all(fixed = TRUE, sequential = FALSE)` uses the same automaton once
there are eight or more patterns.

```{r}
notes <- c("stolen bicycle", "break and enter, tools taken", "graffiti", NA)
keywords <- c("stolen", "taken", "break and enter", "graffiti")
fgrepl_any(keywords, notes)
fwhich_any(keywords, notes)
fextract_any(keywords, notes, all = TRUE)
```

### `fagrepl()` / `fagrep()`

Equivalents of `agrepl()` and `agrep()`: does each string contain something
within `max.distance` edits of a literal `pattern`? Uses Myers' bit-parallel
algorithm. A `max.distance` below 1 is a fraction of the pattern length,
rounded up, as in base R. Regular-expression patterns, custom `costs` and
per-operation limits are passed to base R.

```r
fagrepl(pattern, x, max.distance = 0.1, costs = NULL, ignore.case = FALSE,
        fixed = TRUE, useBytes = FALSE, nthreads = NULL)
fagrep(pattern, x, max.distance = 0.1, costs = NULL, ignore.case = FALSE,
       value = FALSE, fixed = TRUE, useBytes = FALSE, nthreads = NULL)
```

**Returns:** `fagrepl()` a logical vector (`NA` for `NA` input, where base R
gives `FALSE`); `fagrep()` indices, or the matching elements with
`value = TRUE`.

```{r}
x <- c("1 lazy 2", "1 lasy 2", "1 LAZY 2", NA)
fagrepl("lasy", x)
fagrepl("lasy", x, ignore.case = TRUE)
fagrep("lasy", x, value = TRUE)
```

## String utilities

The four base R equivalents (`ftrimws()`, `fsubstr()`, `fnchar()`,
`fchartr()`) preserve `names(x)` and `NA` handling exactly like base R; the
others keep names too.

### `ftrimws()`

```r
ftrimws(x, which = c("both", "left", "right"), whitespace = "[ \t\r\n]")
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `x` | Character vector. `NA` elements return `NA`. |
| `which` | One of `"both"`, `"left"`, `"right"`. |
| `whitespace` | Regex of characters to strip. Only the default `"[ \t\r\n]"` uses the fast path; any other value delegates to `base::trimws()`. |

**Returns:** character vector the same length as `x`, with `names(x)`
preserved.

```{r}
ftrimws(c("  padded  ", "\ttabbed\n"))
ftrimws("  left only", which = "left")
```

### `fsubstr()`

```r
fsubstr(x, start, stop, nthreads = NULL)
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `x` | Character vector. `NA` elements return `NA`. |
| `start`, `stop` | Integer (or numeric) vectors of length 1 or `length(x)`, 1-indexed, clamped to each string's bounds, recycled to `length(x)`. `NA` in either produces `NA` for that element. |
| `nthreads` | Positive integer per-call thread cap, or `NULL` for the RcppParallel default; `1` forces serial execution. |

**Returns:** character vector the same length as `x`.

```{r}
fsubstr("NSWREC123456789", 1, 3)
fsubstr(rep("ABCDEFGH", 3), c(1, 4, 7), c(3, 6, 8))  # vectorised start/stop
```

### `fnchar()`

```r
fnchar(x, type = "chars", allowNA = FALSE, keepNA = NA, nthreads = NULL)
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `x` | Vector, coerced to character via `as.character()` if needed. |
| `type` | One of `"bytes"`, `"chars"`, or `"width"`. `"width"` delegates to `base::nchar()` (display width isn't parallelised). |
| `allowNA` | Logical. Ignored; the fast path never raises an encoding error regardless. |
| `keepNA` | Logical or `NA` (default). `NA`/`TRUE`: `NA` elements of `x` return `NA`. `FALSE`: they return `2L` (length of the string `"NA"`), matching base R's legacy behaviour. |
| `nthreads` | Positive integer per-call thread cap, or `NULL` for the RcppParallel default; `1` forces serial execution. |

**Returns:** integer vector the same length as `x`, with `names(x)`
preserved.

```{r}
fnchar(c("café", "abc", NA))
fnchar(c("café", "abc"), type = "bytes")  # "é" is 2 bytes in UTF-8
```

### `fchartr()`

```r
fchartr(old, new, x, nthreads = NULL)
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `old`, `new` | Single strings with the same number of characters. Each character of `old` maps to the corresponding character of `new`. |
| `x` | Character vector. `NA` elements return `NA`. |
| `nthreads` | Positive integer per-call thread cap, or `NULL` for the RcppParallel default; `1` forces serial execution. |

**Returns:** character vector the same length as `x`. Falls back to
`base::chartr()` automatically when `old`/`new` contain multi-byte
characters (the fast path is a flat byte lookup table, valid only for
single-byte/ASCII characters).

```{r}
fchartr("'-", "  ", c("O'Brien", "Smith-Jones"))
fchartr("aeiou", "AEIOU", "fast string")
```

### `fsquish()`

Trims both ends and collapses internal runs of whitespace to one space,
like `stringr::str_squish()`. Whitespace is Unicode's `White_Space` set
(including the no-break space and the ideographic space).

```r
fsquish(x, nthreads = NULL)
```

```{r}
fsquish(c("  12   Smith\tSt  ", "already clean", NA))
```

### `fsplit_field()`

One field of each string split at `split`, like `stringr::str_split_i()` or
DuckDB's `split_part()`, without building the intermediate list. Every field
counts, including empty ones.

```r
fsplit_field(x, split, field, fixed = FALSE, perl = FALSE,
             ignore.case = FALSE, useBytes = FALSE, nthreads = NULL)
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `split` | The separator: a regular expression unless `fixed = TRUE`; must not match `""`. |
| `field` | Non-zero integer; negative values count from the end (`-1` is the last field). |

**Returns:** character vector, `NA` where the string has fewer fields.

```{r}
x <- c("2024-03-15", "1999-12-31", "bad", NA)
fsplit_field(x, "-", 1, fixed = TRUE)
fsplit_field(x, "-", -1, fixed = TRUE)
```

### `ascii_fold()`

ICU's `"Latin-ASCII"` transliteration (`stringi::stri_trans_general(x,
"Latin-ASCII")`) from a built-in table: accents removed, ligatures and
special letters spelled out, typographic punctuation and spaces made ASCII.
Characters it cannot fold are kept, or replaced by `sub`.

```r
ascii_fold(x, sub = NULL, nthreads = NULL)
```

```{r}
ascii_fold(c("François Müller", "Æsir Ørsted", "Straße"))
ascii_fold("Δι café", sub = "")
```

### `fpad()`

Pads each string to at least `width` characters, like `stringr::str_pad()`.
Width counts characters (code points), so accented text pads correctly.

```r
fpad(x, width, side = c("left", "right", "both"), pad = " ", nthreads = NULL)
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `side` | `"left"` (right-aligns the text), `"right"` or `"both"` (the left gets the smaller half). |
| `pad` | A single character. |

```{r}
fpad(c("800", "4000", "2", NA), 4, pad = "0")
fpad("abc", 7, side = "both", pad = "*")
```

### `freplace_tokens()`

Splits each string at whitespace, replaces every token found in `from` with
the matching element of `to` (`""` deletes it) and joins the tokens with
single spaces. Only whole tokens are replaced; replacements are not
re-scanned. See @sec-uc-clean for dictionaries of abbreviations and
nicknames.

```r
freplace_tokens(x, from, to, ignore_case = FALSE, nthreads = NULL)
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `from` | Tokens to replace: non-empty, no whitespace; the first of any duplicates wins. |
| `to` | Replacements, the same length as `from` or length 1. |
| `ignore_case` | Match regardless of the case of ASCII letters. |

**Returns:** character vector; the result is squished even where nothing is
replaced.

```{r}
freplace_tokens(c("12 SMITH ST", "  7   KING   ST  "), c("ST", "RD"),
                c("STREET", "ROAD"))
freplace_tokens("Dr John Smith", c("dr", "mr"), "", ignore_case = TRUE)
```

### `url_encode()` / `url_decode()`

Percent-encoding as `utils::URLencode()` and decoding as
`utils::URLdecode()`, over whole vectors in parallel. `url_decode()` keeps a
broken escape such as `%zz` as it is, and with `plus = TRUE` decodes `+` as a
space.

```r
url_encode(x, reserved = FALSE, repeated = FALSE, nthreads = NULL)
url_decode(x, plus = FALSE, nthreads = NULL)
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `reserved` | Also encode the reserved characters (for one URL component). |
| `repeated` | Encode strings that already contain `%xx` escapes (`URLencode()` returns them unchanged). |
| `plus` | Decode `+` as a space, as form data and query strings use it. |

```{r}
enc <- url_encode(c("fish & chips", "caf\u00e9 /menu"), reserved = TRUE)
enc
url_decode(enc)
url_decode("q=meat+pie%21", plus = TRUE)
```

### `html_unescape()`

Decodes HTML character references exactly as Python's `html.unescape()`:
all 2,231 named references of the HTML standard (including legacy ones
without a semicolon) and decimal and hexadecimal numeric references, with
the standard's rules for invalid numbers.

```r
html_unescape(x, nthreads = NULL)
```

```{r}
html_unescape(c("Fish &amp; Chips", "caf&eacute; &#8211; open", "AT&T"))
```

## Clustering keys

### `fingerprint()` / `ngram_fingerprint()`

OpenRefine's key-collision keys for grouping spelling variants. The
fingerprint lowercases, decomposes and strips accents and punctuation, then
sorts and de-duplicates the words; the n-gram fingerprint removes all
whitespace and keeps the sorted, de-duplicated character n-grams.

```r
fingerprint(x, nthreads = NULL)
ngram_fingerprint(x, n = 2L, nthreads = NULL)
```

```{r}
x <- c("Smith, John", "john SMITH", "John  Smith.", "Jon Smith")
fingerprint(x)
ngram_fingerprint(c("Acme Pty Ltd", "ACME PtyLtd"))
```

## Parsing, validation and hashing

### `fparse_number()`

The first number in each string, ignoring currency symbols, units, labels
and grouping marks, like `readr::parse_number()`. A minus sign counts even
with a currency symbol or space between it and the digits, but not when it
joins two words (`"SKU-123"` is 123). The value is the correctly rounded
double, as `as.numeric()` would give for the number found.

```r
fparse_number(x, decimal_mark = ".", grouping_mark = ",", nthreads = NULL)
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `decimal_mark` | A single character. |
| `grouping_mark` | Characters allowed between digit groups (`""` for none). |

**Returns:** double vector, `NA` where a string holds no number.

```{r}
fparse_number(c("$1,234.50", "12.5%", "approx. 3,000 kg", "-$45", "n/a"))
fparse_number("1.234,50 EUR", decimal_mark = ",", grouping_mark = ".")
```

### `valid_id()`

Whether each string is a well-formed identifier of the given type: right
length, right characters and a correct check digit, ignoring spaces and
hyphens. Types: `"luhn"` (payment cards, IMEIs, ...), `"abn"`, `"acn"`,
`"tfn"` (9 digits; 8-digit TFNs give `NA`), `"medicare"`, `"isbn"` (10 or
13), `"ean"` (EAN-8, UPC-A, EAN-13, GTIN-14) and `"iban"`. Apart from
Medicare, the rules are tested against `python-stdnum`.

```r
valid_id(x, type = c("luhn", "abn", "acn", "tfn", "medicare", "isbn", "ean", "iban"),
         nthreads = NULL)
```

```{r}
valid_id(c("51 824 753 556", "51 824 753 557"), "abn")
valid_id(c("4111 1111 1111 1111", "4111 1111 1111 1112"), "luhn")
valid_id("GB82 WEST 1234 5698 7654 32", "iban")
```

### `string_shape()`

Each string's pattern of character classes -- `A` for an upper-case letter,
`a` for a lower-case one, `9` for a digit, everything else kept -- for
profiling the formats in a column (@sec-uc-profile). Classes follow Unicode
categories; combining marks are dropped.

```r
string_shape(x, collapse = FALSE, ignore_case = FALSE, nthreads = NULL)
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `collapse` | Collapse each run of `A`, `a` or `9` to one character. |
| `ignore_case` | Map every letter to `a`. |

```{r}
string_shape(c("0412 345 678", "(07) 3123 4567", "QLD 4000", "O'Brien"))
string_shape(c("0412 345 678", "O'Brien"), collapse = TRUE)
```

### `fhash()`

A lower-case hex digest of each string's UTF-8 bytes: SHA-256 (default),
SHA-1, MD5, SHA-512 or the non-cryptographic XXH64. With a `key`, the SHA
and MD5 digests become HMACs, the standard keyed pseudonym
(@sec-uc-privacy). Digests agree with `openssl` and `digest`.

```r
fhash(x, algo = c("sha256", "sha1", "md5", "sha512", "xxh64"), key = NULL,
      seed = 0, nthreads = NULL)
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `key` | Secret for an HMAC: a string or a raw vector. Not allowed with `"xxh64"`. |
| `seed` | Seed for `"xxh64"`. |

```{r}
fhash("abc")
fhash("abc", "md5")
fhash("123456782", key = "secret")
fhash("abc", "xxh64")
```

## Dates

### `format_date()`

```r
format_date(x, format = c("iso", "compact", "dmy", "ymd_slash"),
            nthreads = NULL)
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `x` | A `Date` object or numeric vector of days since 1970-01-01. |
| `format` | `"iso"` (`YYYY-MM-DD`), `"compact"` (`YYYYMMDD`), `"dmy"` (`DD/MM/YYYY`), or `"ymd_slash"` (`YYYY/MM/DD`). |
| `nthreads` | Positive integer per-call thread cap, or `NULL` for the RcppParallel default; `1` forces serial execution. |

**Returns:** character vector the same length as `x`.

```{r}
format_date(as.Date(c("2024-06-18", NA)), "compact")
```

### `format_date_parts()`

Pure string-building (zero-padding plus punctuation, no calendar math, no
`Date` object) — the inverse of `date_parts()`.

```r
format_date_parts(year, month, day,
                  format = c("iso", "compact", "dmy", "ymd_slash"),
                  nthreads = NULL)
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `year`, `month`, `day` | Numeric vectors, recycled to a common length. `NA`, non-integer-coercible, or out-of-width values (year outside 0-9999, month/day outside 0-99) produce `NA` for that element. No calendar validation — `month = 13` formats as given if it fits the field width. |
| `format` | Same four options as `format_date()`. |
| `nthreads` | Positive integer per-call thread cap, or `NULL` for the RcppParallel default; `1` forces serial execution. |

**Returns:** character vector recycled to the common length of `year`,
`month`, `day`.

```{r}
format_date_parts(2024, 6, 18, "iso")
```

### `date_parts()`

```r
date_parts(x, nthreads = NULL)
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `x` | A `Date` object or numeric vector of days since 1970-01-01. |
| `nthreads` | Positive integer per-call thread cap, or `NULL` for the RcppParallel default; `1` forces serial execution. |

**Returns:** a `data.frame` with integer columns `year`, `month`, `day`.

```{r}
date_parts(as.Date(c("2024-06-18", "1999-12-31")))
```

### `fas.Date()`

Reads one fixed format (no locale handling or format guessing) and checks
the full calendar, so impossible dates are `NA` as with `base::as.Date()`.
Numeric `x` is read as counts from a standard epoch (Excel, SAS/Stata,
SPSS, MATLAB, Julian days, ...); see `?fas.Date` for the table.

```r
fas.Date(x, format = c("iso", "compact", "dmy", "ymd_slash"),
         origin = "unix", nthreads = NULL)
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `x` | Character vector, or numeric counts from `origin`. Character elements that don't match `format` exactly (wrong length/separators/non-digits) or are not a real calendar date become `NA`. A `Date` is returned as is; a date-time is converted with `base::as.Date()`. |
| `format` | Same four options as `format_date()`; `x` must be in exactly this one format. |
| `origin` | For numeric `x`: a named epoch (`"unix"`, `"excel"`, `"sas"`, ...) or a day 0 as a `Date` or `"YYYY-MM-DD"` string. |
| `nthreads` | Positive integer per-call thread cap, or `NULL` for the RcppParallel default; `1` forces serial execution. |

**Returns:** a `Date` vector the same length as `x`.

```{r}
fas.Date(c("18/06/2024", "29/02/2023", "not-a-date"), "dmy")
fas.Date(c(1, 60, 45000), origin = "excel")
```

### `fas.POSIXct()`

Parses strict, locale-free timestamps directly into UTC seconds since the
Unix epoch — no timezone-database consultation, no multi-format guessing.
Unlike `fas.Date()`, calendar dates *are* fully validated, including month
lengths and leap years.

```r
fas.POSIXct(x, format = c("iso", "rfc3339", "compact", "iso_offset"),
            nthreads = NULL)
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `x` | Character vector. `NA` elements, malformed values, and out-of-range or impossible calendar dates become `NA`. |
| `format` | `"iso"` (`YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`), `"rfc3339"` (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`), `"compact"` (`YYYYMMDDHHMMSS`), or `"iso_offset"` (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+HH:MM`). |
| `nthreads` | Positive integer per-call thread cap, or `NULL` for the RcppParallel default; `1` forces serial execution. |

**Returns:** a `POSIXct` vector in UTC, the same length as `x`, with
`names(x)` preserved.

```{r}
fas.POSIXct(c("2024-06-18 09:15:00", "not a time"))
fas.POSIXct("2024-06-18T09:15:00Z", "rfc3339")
fas.POSIXct("20240618091500", "compact")
fas.POSIXct("2024-06-18T09:15:00+10:00", "iso_offset")  # normalised to UTC
fas.POSIXct("2023-02-29 08:00:00")                      # NA -- not a leap year
```

### `format_datetime()`

The inverse: formats Unix-epoch seconds without locale or
timezone-database overhead.

```r
format_datetime(x, format = c("iso", "rfc3339", "compact", "iso_offset"),
                offset = "Z", nthreads = NULL)
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `x` | A `POSIXct` object or numeric vector of seconds since 1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC. |
| `format` | The same four formats accepted by `fas.POSIXct()`. |
| `offset` | Fixed offset written by `format = "iso_offset"`: `"Z"`, or a signed `"+HH:MM"`/`"-HH:MM"` string. Must be `"Z"` for the other three formats, which are emitted in UTC. |
| `nthreads` | Positive integer per-call thread cap, or `NULL` for the RcppParallel default; `1` forces serial execution. |

**Returns:** character vector the same length as `x`.

`"iso_offset"` applies one fixed numeric offset to every element. It is not
a timezone — there are no daylight-saving rules — so use `base::format()`
with a real timezone when a series crosses a DST boundary.

```{r}
stamps <- fas.POSIXct(c("2024-06-18 09:15:00", "2024-06-18 23:59:59"))
format_datetime(stamps, "rfc3339")
format_datetime(stamps, "compact")
format_datetime(stamps, "iso_offset", offset = "+10:00")
```

## Phonetic blocking keys

None of these functions has a base R equivalent; all are intended as
blocking keys ahead of fuzzy name matching (@sec-theory, @sec-workflow).

### `soundex()`

```r
soundex(x, nthreads = NULL)
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `x` | Character vector (coerced via `as.character()` if not already character — e.g. a factor read from CSV). `NA` elements, and elements with no alphabetic characters, return `NA`. |
| `nthreads` | Positive integer per-call thread cap, or `NULL` for the RcppParallel default; `1` forces serial execution. |

**Returns:** character vector the same length as `x`, with `names(x)`
preserved; each element either `NA` or exactly 4 characters.

```{r}
soundex(c("Robert", "Rupert", "Ashcraft"))
```

### `nysiis()`

```r
nysiis(x, nthreads = NULL)
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `x` | Character vector (coerced via `as.character()` if needed). `NA` elements, and elements with no alphabetic characters, return `NA`. |
| `nthreads` | Positive integer per-call thread cap, or `NULL` for the RcppParallel default; `1` forces serial execution. |

**Returns:** character vector the same length as `x`, with `names(x)`
preserved; each element either `NA` or up to 6 characters.

```{r}
nysiis(c("Robert", "Rupert", "Ashcraft"))
```

### `refined_soundex()`

The US-English Refined Soundex mapping from Apache Commons Codec. Where
classic `soundex()` discards vowels and truncates to four characters,
Refined Soundex encodes vowels too and emits a code for every change in
phonetic class, with no truncation — a longer, more discriminating key that
produces smaller blocks.

```r
refined_soundex(x, nthreads = NULL)
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `x` | Character vector (coerced via `as.character()` if needed). `NA` elements, and elements with no ASCII letters, return `NA`. |
| `nthreads` | Positive integer per-call thread cap, or `NULL` for the RcppParallel default; `1` forces serial execution. |

**Returns:** character vector the same length as `x`, with `names(x)`
preserved. Code length varies with the input and is **not** truncated —
note that `phonics::refinedSoundex()` caps codes at 10 characters by
default, so the two agree only once its `maxCodeLen` is raised
(@sec-theory).

```{r}
refined_soundex(c("Robert", "Rupert", "Ashcraft"))

# Splits a Soundex block that classic soundex() merges
data.frame(
    name    = c("Smith", "Smyth", "Schmidt", "Sandy"),
    soundex = soundex(c("Smith", "Smyth", "Schmidt", "Sandy")),
    refined = refined_soundex(c("Smith", "Smyth", "Schmidt", "Sandy"))
)
```

### `cologne()`

The Cologne phonetic algorithm (*Kölner Phonetik*), designed for German
pronunciation. Input is uppercased bytewise, umlauts are mapped to their
base vowels, sharp s to `SS`, and remaining non-letters ignored before
encoding — so German spelling variants that ASCII-only schemes split are
grouped together.

```r
cologne(x, nthreads = NULL)
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `x` | Character vector (coerced via `as.character()` if needed). `NA` elements, and elements with no supported letters, return `NA`. |
| `nthreads` | Positive integer per-call thread cap, or `NULL` for the RcppParallel default; `1` forces serial execution. |

**Returns:** character vector the same length as `x`, with `names(x)`
preserved; a digit string, or `NA`.

```{r}
cologne(c("Müller-Lüdenscheidt", "Meier", "Meyer"))

# Umlaut folding: refined_soundex() splits this pair, cologne() doesn't
data.frame(
    name    = c("Müller", "Mueller"),
    refined = refined_soundex(c("Müller", "Mueller")),
    cologne = cologne(c("Müller", "Mueller"))
)
```

### `double_metaphone()`

Two codes per word — `primary` and `secondary` — for ambiguous
pronunciations. Ported from the structure of Apache Commons Codec's
Java implementation and cross-checked against its published test
vectors. Unlike `soundex()`/`nysiis()`, internal whitespace/punctuation
is *not* stripped before encoding (only the ends are trimmed and the
text uppercased) — the algorithm itself keys off literal fragments like
`"VAN "`/`"SCH"`, including the space.

```r
double_metaphone(x, nthreads = NULL)
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `x` | Character vector (coerced via `as.character()` if needed). `NA` elements, and elements with no content after trimming, return `NA` in both columns. |
| `nthreads` | Positive integer per-call thread cap, or `NULL` for the RcppParallel default; `1` forces serial execution. |

**Returns:** a `data.frame` with character columns `primary` and
`secondary`, each `length(x)` long.

```{r}
double_metaphone(c("Smith", "Schmidt", "Catherine", "Kathryn"))
```

### `caverphone()`

Caverphone 2.0 (Caversham Project, University of Otago) — a fixed
10-character code via a chain of substring transforms, widely used in
NZ/AU record linkage. Ported step-for-step from Apache Commons Codec's
`Caverphone2` and cross-checked against its published test vectors,
including the "enough"/"trough" duplicate-rule quirk inherited from the
original 2004 specification (preserved rather than "corrected" — the
point of a phonetic key is to match the standard everyone else uses).

```r
caverphone(x, nthreads = NULL)
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `x` | Character vector (coerced via `as.character()` if needed). `NA` elements return `NA`; every other input — including `""` — returns a 10-character code. |
| `nthreads` | Positive integer per-call thread cap, or `NULL` for the RcppParallel default; `1` forces serial execution. |

**Returns:** character vector the same length as `x`, with `names(x)`
preserved; each element either `NA` or exactly 10 characters.

```{r}
caverphone(c("Peter", "Tedder", "Stevenson"))
```

### `metaphone()`

Lawrence Philips' original Metaphone, as Apache Commons Codec implements it
(which Solr and Elasticsearch use). `phonics::metaphone()` follows PHP's
variant instead.

```r
metaphone(x, max_length = 4L, nthreads = NULL)
```

```{r}
metaphone(c("Thompson", "Knight", "Wright", "Christopher"))
```

### `mra_encode()` / `mra_compare()`

The Western Airlines Match Rating Approach (1977): a codex of at most six
letters, and a pairwise match test, following the published rules as the
Python `jellyfish` package implements them.

```r
mra_encode(x, nthreads = NULL)
mra_compare(a, b, nthreads = NULL)
```

```{r}
mra_encode(c("Byrne", "Boern", "Catherine", "Kathryn"))
mra_compare(c("Byrne", "Michael"), c("Boern", "Mike"))
```

### `statcan()`, `lein()`, `phonex()`, `roger_root()`, `onca()`

Five more name codes from the record-linkage literature. The first four
reproduce the `phonics` package rule for rule (but ignore non-letters
instead of returning `NA`, and fold accents); `onca()` is NYSIIS followed by
Soundex.

```r
statcan(x, max_length = 4L, nthreads = NULL)
lein(x, max_length = 4L, nthreads = NULL)
phonex(x, max_length = 4L, nthreads = NULL)
roger_root(x, max_length = 5L, nthreads = NULL)
onca(x, max_length = 4L, nthreads = NULL)
```

```{r}
x <- c("William", "Peter", "Stevenson", "Stephenson")
data.frame(x, statcan = statcan(x), lein = lein(x), phonex = phonex(x),
           roger_root = roger_root(x), onca = onca(x))
```

## Fuzzy string similarity

### `jaro_winkler()`

Vectorised pairwise Jaro-Winkler similarity. See @sec-theory for the
algorithm and the bit-parallel implementation.

```r
jaro_winkler(a, b, p = 0.1, nthreads = NULL, use_bytes = TRUE)
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `a`, `b` | Equal-length character vectors. |
| `p` | Prefix scaling factor (default `0.1`, the standard value). |
| `nthreads` | Positive integer per-call thread cap, or `NULL` for the RcppParallel default; `1` forces serial execution. |
| `use_bytes` | `TRUE` for compatibility byte comparison; `FALSE` for UTF-8 code points. |

**Returns:** numeric vector of similarities in `[0, 1]`.

```{r}
jaro_winkler(c("MARTHA", "DWAYNE"), c("MARHTA", "DUANE"))
jaro_winkler("SMITH", "SMYTH", p = 0)    # no prefix bonus
jaro_winkler("SMITH", "SMYTH", p = 0.1)  # standard prefix bonus
```

### `jaro_winkler_matrix()`

All-pairs Jaro-Winkler similarity — every element of `a` against every
element of `b`.

```r
jaro_winkler_matrix(a, b, p = 0.1, nthreads = NULL, use_bytes = TRUE)
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `a` | Character vector of length n (rows). |
| `b` | Character vector of length m (columns). |
| `p`, `nthreads` | Same as `jaro_winkler()`. |
| `use_bytes` | Logical. Compare encoded bytes (`TRUE`) or UTF-8 code points (`FALSE`). |

**Returns:** numeric matrix of dimensions n × m.

```{r}
jaro_winkler_matrix(c("JOHN SMITH", "MARY JONES"), c("JON SMYTH", "MARY JONES", "JOHN SMITH"))
```

### `jaro_winkler_tokens()`

Token-reorder- and punctuation-aware Jaro-Winkler similarity. Full
mechanics in @sec-theory.

```r
jaro_winkler_tokens(a, b, p = 0.1, ignore_case = FALSE, strip = "['’-]",
                    extra_penalty = NULL, contractions = FALSE,
                    nthreads = NULL)
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `a`, `b` | Equal-length character vectors. |
| `p` | Prefix scaling factor (default `0.1`). |
| `ignore_case` | Logical (default `FALSE`). Uppercase both sides before comparing. |
| `strip` | Single regex string matching punctuation to remove before tokenising, or `NULL` to skip. Default `"['’-]"` strips straight/curly apostrophes and hyphens. |
| `extra_penalty` | `NULL` (default) or a non-negative numeric scalar. `NULL`: unmatched tokens dilute the average (divide by `max(n_tokens_a, n_tokens_b)`). A number: average over only matched tokens, then subtract `extra_penalty` per unmatched token (floored at 0) — `0` ignores extra tokens outright. |
| `nthreads` | Positive integer per-call thread cap, or `NULL` for the RcppParallel default; `1` forces serial execution. |

**Returns:** numeric vector of similarities in `[0, 1]`. `NA` if either
side of a pair is `NA`.

```{r}
# Reordered tokens, one near-miss — rescued relative to plain jaro_winkler()
jaro_winkler_tokens("Kyle John Haynes", "John Kylie Haynes")
jaro_winkler("Kyle John Haynes", "John Kylie Haynes")

# Punctuation/spacing variants of the same name
jaro_winkler_tokens(c("OBrien", "OBrien"), c("O Brien", "O'Brien"))

# A stray extra token, penalised by default...
jaro_winkler_tokens("Kylie John ZZ Haynes", "Haynes John Kyle")
# ...vs. ignored outright with extra_penalty = 0
jaro_winkler_tokens("Kylie John ZZ Haynes", "Haynes John Kyle", extra_penalty = 0)
# ...vs. lightly discounted
jaro_winkler_tokens("Kylie John ZZ Haynes", "Haynes John Kyle", extra_penalty = 0.1)
```

## Fuzzy lookup

`fuzzy_match()` returns the best table index for every query.
`fuzzy_top_n()` returns a long data frame of ranked candidates. Both scan the
table without allocating a full all-pairs matrix and compare UTF-8 code points
by default.

```r
fuzzy_match(x, table,
            method = c("jaro_winkler", "levenshtein", "osa", "damerau_levenshtein"),
            p = 0.1, min_score = 0, max_distance = NULL, match_na = FALSE,
            nomatch = NA_integer_, nthreads = NULL, use_bytes = FALSE)
fuzzy_top_n(x, table,
            method = c("jaro_winkler", "levenshtein", "osa", "damerau_levenshtein"),
            top_n = 5L, p = 0.1, min_score = 0, max_distance = NULL,
            match_na = FALSE, nthreads = NULL, use_bytes = FALSE)
```

Supported methods are `"jaro_winkler"`, `"levenshtein"`, `"osa"`, and
`"damerau_levenshtein"`. Scores are normalized to `[0, 1]`; ties resolve to
the earliest table position.

```{r}
fuzzy_match(c("SMITH", "JONES"), c("SMYTH", "JONAS", "JONES"))
fuzzy_top_n("kitten", c("sitting", "mitten", "cat"),
            method = "levenshtein", top_n = 2)
```

### `fuzzy_within()`

Every table entry within `max_distance` edits of each query, found with
SymSpell's symmetric-delete index instead of comparing every pair. Candidates
are verified with the exact distance, so the result is exactly the set of
pairs within the cutoff.

```r
fuzzy_within(x, table, max_distance = 1L,
             method = c("osa", "levenshtein", "damerau_levenshtein"),
             prefix_length = 7L, nthreads = NULL, use_bytes = FALSE)
```

**Returns:** a data frame of `query_index`, `table_index` and `distance`.

```{r}
fuzzy_within(c("SMITH", "JONSE"),
             c("SMITH", "SMYTH", "SMITHE", "SIMTH", "JONES", "SMITHS"))
```

### `tfidf_top_n()` / `tfidf_match()`

Cosine similarity of TF-IDF weighted character n-grams, as ING's
`sparse_dot_topn` and `string_grouper` compute it, with the IDF learnt from
`table`. An inverted index means each query only meets the entries it shares
an n-gram with.

```r
tfidf_top_n(x, table, top_n = 5L, q = 3L, min_score = 0, nthreads = NULL,
            use_bytes = FALSE)
tfidf_match(x, table, q = 3L, min_score = 0, nomatch = NA_integer_,
            nthreads = NULL, use_bytes = FALSE)
```

```{r}
companies <- c("ACME PTY LTD", "ACME HOLDINGS PTY LTD", "APEX PTY LTD",
               "BETA INDUSTRIES PTY LTD")
tfidf_top_n(c("ACME LTD", "BETA IND"), companies, top_n = 2)
```

### `minhash_pairs()`

Candidate pairs whose q-gram Jaccard similarity probably reaches
`threshold`, by MinHash signatures and banded locality-sensitive hashing
(as `datasketch`'s `MinHashLSH` and `zoomerjoin`). Bands and rows are chosen
as `datasketch` does; with `verify = TRUE` every pair returned has an exact
Jaccard similarity of at least `threshold`, and `weights = c(0.1, 0.9)`
trades time for fewer missed pairs.

```r
minhash_pairs(x, y = NULL, threshold = 0.5, q = 3L, n_hash = 128L,
              bands = NULL, weights = c(0.5, 0.5), seed = 1, verify = TRUE,
              nthreads = NULL, use_bytes = FALSE)
```

```{r}
x <- c("12 SMITH STREET BRISBANE", "12 SMITH ST BRISBANE",
       "45 JONES ROAD IPSWICH", "45 JONES RD IPSWICH", "7 KING LANE")
minhash_pairs(x, threshold = 0.4)
```

## Blocking and clustering

### `block_pairs()`

Every pair of records that agree exactly on at least one key. Each column of
a data frame is one blocking pass; a pair found by several passes is
reported once, with the first. `NA` keys never pair. With `y`, pairs link
`x` to `y`; without it, pairs are within `x` (`x_index < y_index`).

```r
block_pairs(x, y = NULL, max_block_size = Inf, nthreads = NULL)
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `x`, `y` | A key vector, or a data frame or list of keys (one per pass). |
| `max_block_size` | Skip blocks with more records than this, with a warning. |

**Returns:** data frame with `x_index`, `y_index` and `pass`.

```{r}
people <- data.frame(surname = c("SMITH", "SMYTH", "JONES", "SMITH"),
                     dob = as.Date(c("1980-01-02", "1980-01-02", "1975-06-30",
                                     "1990-12-01")))
block_pairs(data.frame(soundex(people$surname), people$dob))
```

### `sorted_neighbourhood()`

The sorted neighbourhood method: sorts the distinct key values and pairs
records whose values are within `(window - 1) / 2` places of each other (and
records with equal values), as Python's `recordlinkage` does. Several keys
give several passes, as in `block_pairs()`.

```r
sorted_neighbourhood(x, y = NULL, window = 3L, nthreads = NULL)
```

```{r}
surname <- c("SMITH", "SMITHE", "SMYTH", "JONES", "JONSON")
sorted_neighbourhood(surname, window = 3)
```

### `cluster_pairs()`

Entity identifiers from matched pairs: records joined by any chain of pairs
share a cluster (connected components, by union-find). Clusters are
numbered in the order of their lowest-indexed record; records in no pair are
clusters of their own.

```r
cluster_pairs(i, j = NULL, n = NULL)
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `i`, `j` | The two record indices of each pair, or a data frame of pairs as `i`. |
| `n` | Number of records (default: the largest index). |

```{r}
cluster_pairs(c(1, 2, 5), c(2, 4, 6))
```

### `rLink()`

Blocking, comparison and assembly in one call: finds candidate pairs with
`block_pairs()` (or `sorted_neighbourhood()`), scores them with any number of
comparators, and returns one `data.table` of pairs, the columns of both
inputs and the scores. Blocking keys and comparison columns are written as
expressions evaluated against the data, so a phonetic code or a substring
goes in the call rather than into a prepared column. Pass `data_2 = NULL` to
deduplicate one file instead.

```r
rLink(data_1, data_2 = NULL, block = NULL, block_2 = NULL, compare = NULL,
      pairs = NULL, block_method = c("exact", "sorted_neighbourhood"),
      window = 3L, max_block_size = Inf, match_missing = FALSE,
      na_strings = "", force_upper_case = TRUE, normalise = TRUE,
      keep = NULL, suffixes = c("_1", "_2"),
      score_position = c("grouped", "end"), nthreads = NULL,
      verbose = FALSE)
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `data_1`, `data_2` | The inputs, never modified. `data_2 = NULL` deduplicates within `data_1`. |
| `block` | Blocking passes. A top-level `list()` separates passes; `list()` or `c()` within a pass separates the terms joined into one key. |
| `block_2` | Blocking expressions for `data_2`, when the two inputs name or store the same thing differently. A `NULL` pass reuses `block`'s. |
| `compare` | Comparator calls whose first argument is the column, e.g. `jaro_winkler(surname)`. Write `a \| b` for columns named differently. |
| `pairs` | Candidate pairs to score instead of blocking, such as a `minhash_pairs()` result. |
| `block_method`, `window` | Exact key agreement, or the sorted neighbourhood with this window. |
| `max_block_size` | Skip blocks larger than this, with a warning. |
| `match_missing`, `na_strings` | Whether records missing a key term pair with each other, and what counts as missing. |
| `force_upper_case` | Upper-case keys and comparison values. Affects the scores, never the columns returned. |
| `normalise` | Convert each comparator's score so that 1 means an exact match. |
| `keep`, `suffixes`, `score_position` | Which columns to carry, how to distinguish the two sides, and where the scores sit. |
| `verbose` | Print per-stage timings. They are returned as `attr(out, "timings")` either way. |

```{r}
enrol <- data.frame(
    surname = c("SMITH", "JONES", "BROWN", "SMYTH"),
    given   = c("JOHN", "MARY", "ROB", "JON"),
    dob     = as.Date(c("1980-01-02", "1975-06-30", "1990-12-01",
                        "1980-01-02"))
)
claims <- data.frame(
    surname = c("SMITH", "JONSE", "BROWNE"),
    given   = c("JON", "MARY", "ROBERT"),
    dob     = as.Date(c("1980-01-02", "1975-06-30", "1990-12-01"))
)

out <- rLink(
    enrol, claims,
    block   = list(list(soundex(surname), dob), fsubstr(given, 1, 2)),
    compare = list(jaro_winkler(given), sn = jaro_winkler(surname))
)
as.data.frame(out[, c("index_1", "index_2", "pass", "surname_1", "surname_2",
                      "sn", "given_jaro_winkler")])
```

Comparators disagree about which end of their scale is an exact match, so
each is probed once and converted where needed: `jaro_winkler()` already
returns 1, the edit distances return 0, and the `fuzz_*` scorers return 100.
With `normalise = TRUE` (the default) 1 always means an exact match, and an
unbounded edit distance is divided pairwise by the longer of the two strings.

```{r}
rLink(enrol, claims, block = list(soundex(surname)),
      compare = list(lev = levenshtein(surname),
                     jw  = jaro_winkler(surname),
                     fz  = fuzz_ratio(surname)))$lev
```

## Edit distance

The edit-distance family distinguishes OSA from unrestricted
Damerau-Levenshtein and offers normalized and bounded forms. Byte comparison
is the compatibility default; `use_bytes = FALSE` compares UTF-8 code points.

### `levenshtein()`

```r
levenshtein(a, b, nthreads = NULL, use_bytes = TRUE, weights = c(1, 1, 1))
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `a`, `b` | Equal-length character vectors. |
| `nthreads` | Positive integer per-call thread cap, or `NULL` for the RcppParallel default; `1` forces serial execution. |
| `use_bytes` | `TRUE` for encoded bytes; `FALSE` for UTF-8 code points. |
| `weights` | Costs of an insertion, a deletion and a substitution (as RapidFuzz's `weights`); also accepted by `levenshtein_matrix()` and `levenshtein_similarity()`. |

**Returns:** numeric vector the same length as `a` (minimum number of
single-character insertions/deletions/substitutions). `NA` if either side
of a pair is `NA`.

```{r}
levenshtein("kitten", "sitting")
```

### `levenshtein_matrix()`

All-pairs Levenshtein distance.

```r
levenshtein_matrix(a, b, nthreads = NULL, use_bytes = TRUE)
```

**Returns:** numeric matrix of dimensions `length(a)` x `length(b)`.

```{r}
levenshtein_matrix(c("kitten", "cat"), c("sitting", "bat"))
```

### `osa_distance()` / `osa_distance_matrix()`

Adjacent transpositions cost one edit under the Optimal String Alignment
restriction that no substring is edited more than once.

```r
osa_distance(a, b, nthreads = NULL, use_bytes = TRUE)
osa_distance_matrix(a, b, nthreads = NULL, use_bytes = TRUE)
```

Arguments identical to `levenshtein()`. **Returns:** numeric vector the
same length as `a`.

```{r}
osa_distance("ca", "abc")  # 3
```

### `damerau_levenshtein()` / `damerau_levenshtein_matrix()`

Unrestricted Damerau-Levenshtein permits a substring to participate in
multiple edits and matches `stringdist(method = "dl")`.

```r
damerau_levenshtein(a, b, nthreads = NULL, use_bytes = TRUE)
damerau_levenshtein_matrix(a, b, nthreads = NULL, use_bytes = TRUE)
```

```{r}
damerau_levenshtein("ca", "abc")  # 2
```

### Normalized and bounded edit comparison

`levenshtein_similarity()`, `osa_similarity()`, and
`damerau_levenshtein_similarity()` return `1 - distance/max(lengths)`.
`levenshtein_within()` uses a banded dynamic program to test a raw cutoff.

```r
levenshtein_similarity(a, b, nthreads = NULL, use_bytes = TRUE)
levenshtein_within(a, b, max_distance, nthreads = NULL, use_bytes = TRUE)
```

### `hamming()`

Number of positions at which two equal-length strings differ.

```r
hamming(a, b, nthreads = NULL, use_bytes = TRUE)
```

Arguments identical to `levenshtein()`. **Returns:** numeric vector the
same length as `a`; `Inf` for a pair of unequal length (matching
`stringdist::stringdist(method = "hamming")`).

```{r}
hamming("karolin", "kathrin")
hamming("abc", "ab")  # Inf -- unequal length
```

### `edit_ops()`

The edits that turn each `a[i]` into `b[i]`, as RapidFuzz's
`Levenshtein.editops()` / `opcodes()` list them, choosing the same
alignment when several are equally short. Positions are 1-based.

```r
edit_ops(a, b, type = c("editops", "opcodes"), use_bytes = FALSE)
```

```{r}
edit_ops("kitten", "sitting")
edit_ops("kitten", "sitting", type = "opcodes")
```

### `lcs_seq_distance()` and relatives

The rest of RapidFuzz's distance module: `lcs_seq_distance()` /
`lcs_seq_similarity()` (longest common subsequence), `indel_distance()` /
`indel_similarity()` (insertions and deletions only; the similarity is
`fuzz_ratio() / 100`), and `prefix_*()` / `postfix_*()` (common prefix or
suffix). All take `(a, b, nthreads = NULL, use_bytes = FALSE)`.

```{r}
lcs_seq_distance("kitten", "sitting")
indel_similarity("kitten", "sitting")
prefix_similarity(c("Johnson", "Johnston"), c("Johnston", "Jonson"))
```

### `editex()` / `editex_similarity()`

Zobel and Dart's Editex: an edit distance in which letters that sound alike
cost less to swap, following the `abydos` and `textdistance` packages.

```{r}
editex(c("Phillips", "Smith"), c("Filips", "Smyth"))
editex_similarity("Niall", "Neil")
```

### `lcs_str()` / `lcs_str_similarity()`

The longest common substring (contiguous), choosing the one that starts
earliest in `a`, as `difflib`'s `find_longest_match()` does.

```{r}
lcs_str("acme holdings pty ltd", "acme holdings limited")
```

### `smith_waterman()`

Smith-Waterman local alignment with Gotoh's affine gaps; the defaults
reproduce SimMetrics' `SmithWatermanGotoh`.

```r
smith_waterman(a, b, match = 1, mismatch = -2, gap_open = -0.5,
               gap_extend = gap_open, normalize = TRUE, nthreads = NULL,
               use_bytes = FALSE)
```

```{r}
smith_waterman("Dept of Health", "Queensland Health")
```

### `monge_elkan()`

The mean, over the words of `a[i]`, of the best similarity to a word of
`b[i]` (Jaro-Winkler by default); `symmetric = TRUE` averages both
directions.

```r
monge_elkan(a, b, method = c("jaro_winkler", "levenshtein", "osa",
                             "damerau_levenshtein"),
            p = 0.1, symmetric = FALSE, nthreads = NULL, use_bytes = FALSE)
```

```{r}
monge_elkan("Smith John", "Jon Smyth")
monge_elkan("Smith", "John Smith", symmetric = TRUE)
```

## Q-gram similarity

`jaccard_index()`, `dice_coefficient()`, `tversky_index()`, and
`cosine_similarity()` compare two strings' overlapping length-`q`
substrings ("q-grams"). All four share one sorted-merge pass over
packed-integer q-grams without routing through `stringdist`'s generic
R-level dispatch (@sec-benchmarks). The first three compare q-gram *sets*
(a repeated q-gram counts once); `cosine_similarity()` compares frequency
profiles, so repetition carries weight.

### `jaccard_index()`

```r
jaccard_index(a, b, q = 2, nthreads = NULL, use_bytes = TRUE)
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `a`, `b` | Equal-length character vectors. |
| `q` | Q-gram length (default `2`, i.e. bigrams). Must be a single integer >= 1. |
| `nthreads` | Positive integer per-call thread cap, or `NULL` for the RcppParallel default; `1` forces serial execution. |
| `use_bytes` | Logical. Compare encoded bytes (`TRUE`) or UTF-8 code points (`FALSE`). |

**Returns:** numeric vector of similarities in `[0, 1]`, `length(a)`
long. Two strings shorter than `q` (so neither has any q-grams) compare
equal (`1`).

```{r}
jaccard_index("night", "nacht")
```

### `jaccard_matrix()`

All-pairs Jaccard similarity. Same argument/return shape as
`jaro_winkler_matrix()`.

```r
jaccard_matrix(a, b, q = 2, nthreads = NULL, use_bytes = TRUE)
```

### `dice_coefficient()` / `dice_matrix()`

The Sorensen-Dice coefficient: `2*|intersection| / (|A| + |B|)`. Weights
shared q-grams more heavily than Jaccard (always `>=` the Jaccard score
for the same pair). Same arguments as `jaccard_index()`/`jaccard_matrix()`.

```{r}
dice_coefficient("night", "nacht")
```

### `tversky_index()` / `tversky_matrix()`

Generalises both: `|intersection| / (|intersection| + alpha*|A only| +
beta*|B only|)`. `alpha = beta = 1` reduces to Jaccard; `alpha = beta =
0.5` (the default) reduces to Dice.

```r
tversky_index(a, b, q = 2, alpha = 0.5, beta = 0.5, nthreads = NULL,
              use_bytes = TRUE)
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `a`, `b`, `q`, `nthreads` | Same as `jaccard_index()`. |
| `alpha`, `beta` | Tversky asymmetry weights (default `0.5` each). Non-negative scalars. |
| `use_bytes` | Logical. Compare encoded bytes (`TRUE`) or UTF-8 code points (`FALSE`). |

```{r}
tversky_index("night", "nacht", alpha = 1, beta = 1)   # == jaccard_index()
tversky_index("night", "nacht", alpha = 0.5, beta = 0.5) # == dice_coefficient()
```

### `cosine_similarity()` / `cosine_matrix()`

Builds a q-gram *frequency profile* for each string and returns the cosine
of the angle between the two profiles — `dot(A, B) / (||A|| * ||B||)`.
Repeated q-grams keep their multiplicity, which is the whole difference
from the three set metrics above.

```r
cosine_similarity(a, b, q = 2, nthreads = NULL, use_bytes = TRUE)
cosine_matrix(a, b, q = 2, nthreads = NULL, use_bytes = TRUE)
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `a`, `b`, `q`, `nthreads` | Same as `jaccard_index()`/`jaccard_matrix()`. |
| `use_bytes` | Logical. Compare encoded bytes (`TRUE`) or UTF-8 code points (`FALSE`). |

**Returns:** numeric vector of similarities in `[0, 1]`, `length(a)` long
(or a `length(a)` × `length(b)` matrix). Missing comparisons return `NA`.
If neither string has a q-gram the similarity is `1`; if only one does,
it is `0`.

```{r}
cosine_similarity("night", "nacht")

# Multiplicity: one distinct shared bigram, but different counts
cosine_similarity("aaaa", "aaab", q = 2)
jaccard_index("aaaa", "aaab", q = 2)

cosine_matrix(c("JOHN SMITH", "MARY JONES"), c("JON SMYTH", "MARY JONES"))
```

## RapidFuzz scorers

Vectorised ports of the scorers in Python's
[RapidFuzz](https://github.com/rapidfuzz/RapidFuzz) `fuzz` module, the
maintained successor to fuzzywuzzy. Scores agree with `rapidfuzz.fuzz` to
floating-point precision; see @sec-theory for the algorithms.

```r
fuzz_ratio(a, b, full_process = TRUE, score_cutoff = 0, nthreads = NULL)
fuzz_partial_ratio(a, b, full_process = TRUE, score_cutoff = 0, nthreads = NULL)
fuzz_token_sort_ratio(a, b, full_process = TRUE, score_cutoff = 0, nthreads = NULL)
fuzz_token_set_ratio(a, b, full_process = TRUE, score_cutoff = 0, nthreads = NULL)
fuzz_token_ratio(a, b, full_process = TRUE, score_cutoff = 0, nthreads = NULL)
fuzz_partial_token_sort_ratio(a, b, full_process = TRUE, score_cutoff = 0, nthreads = NULL)
fuzz_partial_token_set_ratio(a, b, full_process = TRUE, score_cutoff = 0, nthreads = NULL)
fuzz_partial_token_ratio(a, b, full_process = TRUE, score_cutoff = 0, nthreads = NULL)
fuzz_wratio(a, b, full_process = TRUE, score_cutoff = 0, nthreads = NULL)
fuzz_qratio(a, b, full_process = TRUE, score_cutoff = 0, nthreads = NULL)
fuzz_partial_ratio_alignment(a, b, full_process = TRUE, score_cutoff = 0, nthreads = NULL)
fuzz_default_process(x, nthreads = NULL)
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `a`, `b` | Equal-length character vectors. |
| `full_process` | Logical (default `TRUE`). Runs both strings through `fuzz_default_process()` first: lowercase, every character that is not a letter or digit turned into a space, ends trimmed. This is RapidFuzz's `processor = utils.default_process`; `FALSE` compares the strings as given, RapidFuzz's own default. |
| `score_cutoff` | Number in `[0, 100]` (default 0). Scores below it are returned as 0, and the scorers use it to stop early. |
| `nthreads` | Positive integer per-call thread cap, or `NULL` for the RcppParallel default; `1` forces serial execution. |

**Returns:** numeric vector of unrounded scores in `[0, 100]`,
`length(a)` long; `NA` where either input is `NA`.
`fuzz_partial_ratio_alignment()` returns a data frame of the score and
the 1-based positions of the aligned slices (`src_start`, `src_end` in
`a`; `dest_start`, `dest_end` in `b`), and `fuzz_default_process()` the
processed strings.

- **`fuzz_ratio()`**: normalised Indel similarity,
  `200 * LCS / (len(a) + len(b))`.
- **`fuzz_partial_ratio()`**: the best `fuzz_ratio()` of the shorter
  string against any window of the longer one (found exactly).
- **`fuzz_token_sort_ratio()`**: `fuzz_ratio()` of the sorted words.
- **`fuzz_token_set_ratio()`**: compares shared words with each side's
  extra words; 100 when one side's words are a subset of the other's.
- **`fuzz_token_ratio()`**: the better of token sort and token set.
- **`fuzz_partial_token_sort_ratio()`**, **`fuzz_partial_token_set_ratio()`**,
  **`fuzz_partial_token_ratio()`**: the same with the partial ratio.
- **`fuzz_wratio()`**: RapidFuzz's `WRatio`, a length-aware weighted best
  of the above.
- **`fuzz_qratio()`**: `fuzz_ratio()`, but 0 when either string is empty.

The `process` module is ported as well. Each string is processed once, not
once per pair, and the extract functions prune candidates that cannot make
a query's list:

```r
fuzz_extract(x, choices, scorer = "wratio", limit = 5L, full_process = TRUE,
             score_cutoff = 0, nthreads = NULL)
fuzz_extract_one(x, choices, scorer = "wratio", full_process = TRUE,
                 score_cutoff = 0, nthreads = NULL)
fuzz_cdist(x, choices = x, scorer = "ratio", full_process = TRUE,
           score_cutoff = 0, nthreads = NULL)
fuzz_cpdist(a, b, scorer = "ratio", full_process = TRUE, score_cutoff = 0,
            nthreads = NULL)
```

`scorer` is a scorer's name (`"ratio"`, `"token_set_ratio"`, `"wratio"`,
...; RapidFuzz spellings like `"WRatio"` work too) or the function itself.
`fuzz_extract()` returns a long data frame (`query_index`,
`choice_index`, `choice`, `score`, `rank`) of each query's `limit` best
choices (`limit = NULL` for all), with ties in table order.
`fuzz_extract_one()` returns one row per query, `NA` when nothing reaches
`score_cutoff`. `fuzz_cdist()` returns the full score matrix and
`fuzz_cpdist()` element-wise scores.

```{r}
fuzz_ratio("this is a test", "this is a test!")
fuzz_partial_ratio("fuzzy wuzzy was a bear", "wuzzy fuzzy was a bear")
fuzz_token_sort_ratio("fuzzy was a bear", "bear was a fuzzy")
fuzz_token_set_ratio("fuzzy was a bear", "fuzzy fuzzy bear was a bear")
fuzz_wratio("New York Mets", "The New York Mets baseball club")
fuzz_partial_ratio_alignment("a certain string", "cetain", full_process = FALSE)

teams <- c("Atlanta Falcons", "New York Jets", "New York Giants",
           "Dallas Cowboys")
fuzz_extract("new york jets", teams, limit = 2)
fuzz_extract_one(c("cowboys", "falcon"), teams)
round(fuzz_cdist(c("new york", "dallas"), teams, scorer = "token_set_ratio"), 1)
```
